evidence_used: Object image showing a smooth, flat-backed electronic tablet device with an anodized aluminum casing.
Gecko embodiment specification requiring flat, parallel, smooth, nonporous surfaces for optimal mushroom-tipped dry-adhesive pad contact.
Visual scale indicating a medium-sized device of moderate mass.
calculation_summary: Force estimated via baseline scaling for a smooth metal surface: F_normal = F_base_flat * (estimated_weight_scaling), set to 1.5 N given high compatibility and strong dry-adhesive engagement on flat aluminum.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: No authoritative mass or friction coefficient was measured.
Sidewalls of the target object are assumed to be sufficiently flat and parallel to mate cleanly with the rigid parallel-jaw gecko pads.
Visual scale and estimated weight carry standard zero-shot estimation uncertainty.
reasoning_trace: The query displays a smooth, flat metal electronic device casing (tablet/laptop lid) with high compatibility for the rigid mushroom-tipped gecko-inspired dry-adhesive pads. Because the surface is exceptionally smooth, clean, and flat, the gecko adhesive performs near its maximum capability, allowing for a lower normal force requirement to achieve adequate normal preload and friction/adhesion for lifting. Without explicit mass measurements, visual cues suggest a moderate device weight, so a modest normal force of 1.5 N is estimated to securely hold the object without slipping.
